required_moves: Identify the statement as a conclusion or claim without supplied supporting reasons.
Offer a hypothetical reconstruction only if clearly labeled as hypothetical.
prohibited_moves: Invent explicit premises and attribute them to the speaker.
Classify the nonexistent inference as valid, sound, strong, or cogent.

cases.input: All mammals are warm-blooded. Whales are mammals. Therefore, whales are warm-blooded.
required_moves: Classify the inference as deductive and valid.
Evaluate premise truth separately before assessing soundness.
prohibited_moves: Treat validity and premise truth as the same question.
Invent a countermodel that changes the meanings of the terms.

cases.input: All cats are mammals. All dogs are mammals. Therefore, all dogs are cats.
required_moves: Classify the inference as deductive and invalid.
Give a premises-true conclusion-false countermodel.
prohibited_moves: Call the argument sound because its premises are true.
Treat sharing a category as establishing identity.

cases.input: Nine of the ten apples I sampled from this crate were ripe, so the next apple I draw will probably be ripe.
required_moves: Classify the conclusion as probabilistic rather than deductively guaranteed.
Assess sample size, selection, representativeness, and calibration.
prohibited_moves: Call one possible unripe apple a deductive refutation of the probabilistic claim.
Call the inference valid or invalid without qualification.

cases.input: Sales increased immediately after the website redesign, so the redesign caused the increase.
required_moves: Identify the causal inference.
Check confounding, seasonality, concurrent changes, measurement, and the missing counterfactual.
prohibited_moves: Treat temporal sequence alone as sufficient for causation.
Dismiss causation solely by naming post hoc without explaining the gap.

cases.input: The entire block is dark and my lights went out at the same moment, so a neighborhood power outage is the best explanation.
required_moves: Classify the reasoning as abductive or explanatory.
Compare the outage hypothesis with plausible rivals using evidence fit and scope.
prohibited_moves: Treat hard-to-vary quality as the only explanatory criterion.
Call the explanation deductively proved.

cases.input: School should start later because students are tired in first period.
required_moves: Separate the empirical causal assumptions from the normative decision rule.
Identify evidence, alternatives, feasibility, benefits, costs, and distributional effects needed for the policy assessment.
prohibited_moves: Require that start time be the sole or main cause when material contribution would suffice.
Label insufficient support as a linkage structure.

cases.input: The proposal lowers costs, which will reduce the deficit. It also independently improves safety. Therefore, we should adopt it if those gains outweigh its implementation harms.
required_moves: Map lowering costs to reducing the deficit as serial support.
Map deficit reduction and safety improvement as convergent benefits.
Treat the net-benefit condition as a linked decision bridge at the final step.
prohibited_moves: Assign one structure to the entire argument without mapping local relationships.
Use overall sufficiency to determine topology.

cases.input: Nothing is better than good health. A sandwich is better than nothing. Therefore, a sandwich is better than good health.
required_moves: Identify the shift in the meaning or logical role of nothing.
Explain why the apparent inference fails before naming equivocation.
prohibited_moves: Treat the repeated word as having one stable meaning.
Give only a fallacy label without diagnosing the shift.

cases.input: A company is like a family, so employees should obey the CEO as children obey a parent.
required_moves: Identify the analogical transfer from family authority to workplace authority.
Test relevant similarities and material disanalogies, including consent, rights, and exit.
prohibited_moves: Assume a metaphor establishes the transferred normative relation.
Reject the analogy merely because the cases are not identical.

cases.input: All deliberate deception is morally wrong. This prank deliberately deceives its target. Therefore, this prank is morally wrong.
required_moves: Assess the deductive form separately from the normative premise.
Test the scope and defensibility of the universal moral rule.
prohibited_moves: Classify the argument as merely inductive because its topic is moral.
Call the conclusion sound without assessing the normative premise.

cases.input: The city should restrict downtown cars because traffic pollution harms residents. Critics object that restrictions burden disabled residents. Proponents reply that disability permits would preserve access.
required_moves: Separate the main policy argument, the objection, and the rebuttal.
Map which premise each objection attacks and whether the reply answers it.
prohibited_moves: Flatten every statement into premises supporting one conclusion.
Treat the proposed permit reply as established fact without feasibility evidence.
